The Pile is a 825 GiB diverse, open source language modelling data set that consists of 22 smaller, high-quality datasets combined together.

atoms.reference: 22 diverse subsets, existing and newly constructed, many from academic or professional sources; books, movie transcripts and scientific papers among other media; per Wikipedia's table Pile-CC 243.87, Books3 108.40, GitHub 102.18, PubMed Central 96.93, Gutenberg (PG-19) 11.68, total 886.03 (GB).

atoms.span: The Pile is an 825 GiB to 886 GB open-source English text dataset created by EleutherAI
created by EleutherAI and released on December 31, 2020
open-source English text dataset created by EleutherAI and released on December 31, 2020, to train large language models (LLMs).
Combines 22 diverse sub-datasets across academic, web, prose, and code domains.
Designed to improve cross-domain knowledge, reasoning, and generalization compared to raw web scrapes like Common Crawl.

observations.notes: The dataset composed at its grain and itemized to its twenty-two components, the training layer named as the census row names it. Its literary component is glossed by genre, and the pirated source, the removal and the authors' suit that put works in it under their authors' names are reduced to 'content adjustments'.
